Pledge, agreement, deposit and disbursement are different stages of support

01What does this evidence establish?

Saudi support is recorded by stage. A pledge, commitment, signed agreement, deposited amount, amount made available, budget disbursement, FX-auction use, in-kind support and project cost are not interchangeable, and they are not added into a cumulative total here.

01What does this evidence establish?02What does it measure?03Who or what does it apply to?04How current is it?05What this evidence does not establish06Original source and verification07Method and verification detail

02What does it measure?

This record sets out a distinction and reports no value: a pledge, commitment, signed agreement, deposit, amount made available, budget disbursement, use in foreign-exchange auctions, in-kind support and project cost are different stages of Saudi support to Yemen.

03Who or what does it apply to?

Specific to each source or funding or support package

04How current is it?

The evidence in this record spans 2010 to 2026. It should not be read as describing later support unless newer evidence is published.

05What this evidence does not establish

Adding unlike or overlapping stages does not produce a cumulative total of Saudi support, and no such total is established here.

Limits of the measure

No single, fully reconciled public ledger of the flows exists; larger packages and their components, and the commitment, deposit, availability, disbursement and use stages, can overlap.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Evidence from donor and multilateral sources, read with AidData's historical method for classifying Saudi support to Yemen; the stages are kept separate and are not added together.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
